content: Fosfomycin is an antibiotic commonly used to treat bladder infections, such as acute cystitis or lower urinary tract infections, particularly in women. It works by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis, effectively stopping bacterial growth. This medication is specifically effective against bacterial infections and does not treat viral infections like the common cold or flu. Dosage and Administration: Fosfomycin is typically prescribed as a single oral dose of 3 grams, which is provided in a sachet. To prepare the medication, dissolve the contents of one sachet in 4 ounces (120 milliliters) of cold water and stir until fully dissolved. Do not use warm or hot water. The medication should be taken as directed by your doctor, and symptoms should improve within 2 to 3 days. If symptoms persist or worsen, consult your healthcare provider. Indications and Limitations: Fosfomycin is effective for treating uncomplicated urinary tract infections caused by bacteria such as E. coli and E. faecalis. It is not indicated for more severe infections, such as perinephric abscesses or pyelonephritis. For multi-drug-resistant urinary tract infections, fosfomycin may be prescribed at 2-3 grams every 2-3 days for three doses or as part of a longer regimen. However, it is not recommended for persistent or recurrent bacteriuria without further evaluation. Drug Interactions: Fosfomycin can interact with several medications and vaccines: Live bacterial vaccines (e.g., BCG, typhoid, cholera): Fosfomycin reduces their efficacy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic treatment is completed. Oral contraceptives and hormone therapies (e.g., estradiol, conjugated estrogens): Fosfomycin may reduce their effectiveness by altering intestinal flora. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, monitoring is advised. Digoxin: Fosfomycin may increase digoxin levels by altering gut flora. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Other antibiotics or probiotics: Fosfomycin may reduce the efficacy of probiotics or other medications that rely on gut bacteria for activation (e.g., sodium picosulfate). Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating probiotics. Side Effects: Common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, headache, dizziness, fatigue, and rash. Rare but serious side effects include hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis) and liver injury, such as hepatitis or steatosis. If hypersensitivity symptoms occur, discontinue the medication immediately and seek medical attention. Prolonged use may lead to bacterial or fungal superinfections, which can appear up to two months after treatment. Precautions: Allergies: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to fosfomycin or any of its components. Kidney infections: If symptoms such as flank pain, fever, or chills develop, contact your doctor immediately. Dizziness: Fosfomycin may cause dizziness, which can be exacerbated by alcohol or cannabis. Dietary considerations: This product may contain sugar or aspartame, so caution is advised for individuals with diabetes or phenylketonuria (PKU). Pregnancy and Lactation: Fosfomycin is classified as Pregnancy Category B, meaning it is generally considered safe during pregnancy when clearly needed. It is excreted in small amounts in breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Consult your doctor before use if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Storage: Store fosfomycin at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your pharmacist. Overdose: In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., contact Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Additional Information: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not share it with others. Laboratory tests, such as urine cultures, may be performed during treatment to monitor its effectiveness. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
